drafts.proof_strategy: A common point lets one translate each orbit into the other.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose z lies in both orbits and write z = gx = hy.
derive: Then x = g⁻¹hy, so the orbit of x lies in the orbit of y.
derive: The reverse inclusion follows by symmetry.
conclude: Orbits with a common point coincide.

drafts.canonical_statement: Orbit-stabilizer theorem: for an action of a finite group G and a point x, the size of the orbit of x times the size of the stabilizer of x equals |G|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_orbit"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_stabilizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Identify the orbit with the left cosets of the stabilizer and apply Lagrange.
sketch_steps: translate: gx = hx is equivalent to gG_x = hG_x.
construct: The map gG_x ↦ gx is a bijection onto the orbit.
derive: Hence the orbit size equals the index of the stabilizer.
apply_theorem: Lagrange gives the product formula.

drafts.canonical_statement: Burnside's lemma: for a finite group G acting on a finite set X, the sum over g in G of the number of points fixed by g equals the number of orbits times |G|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_fixed_points"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_orbit_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Double count pairs (g, x) with gx = x and use orbit-stabilizer.
sketch_steps: setup: Consider the set of pairs (g, x) with gx = x.
derive: Counting by g gives the sum of |X^g|.
derive: Counting by x gives the sum of |G_x|.
apply_theorem: Orbit-stabilizer gives |G_x| = |G|/|Gx|.
derive: Each orbit contributes exactly |G| to the sum.
conclude: The sum equals |G| times the number of orbits.

drafts.canonical_statement: Cayley's theorem: every group G admits an injective homomorphism into the symmetric group on G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_hom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="injective_function"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the left regular action.
sketch_steps: construct: Send g to left multiplication L_g.
derive: L_g is a permutation with inverse L_{g⁻¹}.
derive: L_{gh} = L_g L_h, so the map is a homomorphism.
derive: Evaluating at 1 shows injectivity.

drafts.canonical_statement: Class equation: for a finite group G, |G| equals |Z(G)| plus the sum of the sizes of the conjugacy classes with more than one element.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_center"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noncentral_conjugacy_classes"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Partition G into conjugacy classes and separate the singleton classes.
sketch_steps: translate: Conjugacy classes partition G.
derive: A class is a singleton exactly when its element is central.
derive: Singleton classes contribute |Z(G)| in total.
conclude: Add the remaining classes to obtain the equation.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p and a positive integer n, the center of a group of order p^n is nontrivial.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="gt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_center"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce the class equation modulo p.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Write the class equation for G.
derive: Each non-singleton class has size a positive power of p.
derive: Therefore p divides |Z(G)|.
conclude: Since |Z(G)| ≥ 1, it is at least p.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p, every group of order p² is abelian.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="abelian_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Combine the nontrivial center of a p-group with the cyclic quotient criterion.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The center of a p-group is nontrivial.
case_split: The center has order p or p².
derive: If it has order p, the quotient G/Z(G) is cyclic of order p.
contradiction: A cyclic quotient by the center forces G to be abelian, so Z(G) = G.
conclude: Therefore Z(G) = G.

drafts.canonical_statement: Cauchy's theorem: if a prime p divides the order of a finite group G, then G has an element of order p.

drafts.proof_strategy: Let Z/p act by cyclic shift on p-tuples with product 1 and count fixed points modulo p.
sketch_steps: setup: Let S be the set of p-tuples of elements of G with product 1.
derive: |S| = |G|^(p-1) is divisible by p.
construct: Cyclic shift gives an action of Z/p on S.
derive: Orbits have size 1 or p, so the number of fixed points is divisible by p.
derive: Fixed points are constant tuples (x, ..., x) with x^p = 1.
conclude: Since (1, ..., 1) is fixed, some x ≠ 1 satisfies x^p = 1, and it has order p.

drafts.canonical_statement: Sylow's first theorem: if p is prime and p^n divides the order of a finite group G, then G has a subgroup of order p^n.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the exponent, enlarging a p-subgroup inside its normalizer via Cauchy's theorem.
sketch_steps: induction: Start from the trivial subgroup and assume H has order p^k.
setup: Let H act on the left cosets of H.
derive: The fixed points correspond to N_G(H)/H and their number is congruent to [G:H] modulo p.
derive: Hence p divides the order of N_G(H)/H.
apply_theorem: Cauchy gives a subgroup of order p in N_G(H)/H.
construct: Its preimage in N_G(H) has order p^(k+1).

drafts.canonical_statement: Sylow's second theorem: any two Sylow p-subgroups of a finite group are conjugate.

drafts.proof_strategy: Let one Sylow subgroup act on the cosets of the other and find a fixed point modulo p.
sketch_steps: setup: Let Q act on the left cosets of P by left multiplication.
derive: The number of fixed points is congruent to [G:P] modulo p, which is nonzero.
construct: Take a fixed coset gP.
derive: Then g⁻¹Qg is contained in P.
conclude: Equal orders give Q = gPg⁻¹.

drafts.proof_strategy: Count fixed points of P acting by conjugation, then use transitivity of G.
sketch_steps: setup: Let P act by conjugation on the set of Sylow p-subgroups.
derive: A fixed point Q has P in its normalizer, and then P = Q.
apply_theorem: The count is congruent modulo p to the number of fixed points, which is 1.
apply_theorem: The second theorem makes G act transitively, so n_p = [G:N_G(P)].
conclude: Since P ≤ N_G(P), n_p divides [G:P] = m.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a finite group has exactly one Sylow p-subgroup, then that subgroup is normal.

drafts.proof_strategy: Conjugates of a Sylow subgroup are Sylow subgroups.
sketch_steps: derive: Each conjugate gSg⁻¹ has the same order as S, so it is a Sylow p-subgroup.
derive: Uniqueness gives gSg⁻¹ = S.
conclude: S is normal.

drafts.canonical_statement: A group homomorphism from a simple group is either trivial or injective.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_hom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="or"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_kernel"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="injective_function"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply simplicity to the kernel.
sketch_steps: translate: The kernel of f is a normal subgroup of G.
case_split: Simplicity makes it trivial or all of G.
conclude: These cases give injective and trivial respectively.

drafts.canonical_statement: An abelian group is simple if and only if its order is prime.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="abelian_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: In an abelian group every subgroup is normal, so simplicity means no proper nontrivial subgroups.
sketch_steps: translate: In an abelian group all subgroups are normal.
derive: A simple abelian group is generated by any non-identity element, so it is cyclic.
derive: The infinite cyclic group has the subgroup 2Z, so G is finite.
derive: A cyclic group of composite order has a proper nontrivial subgroup, so the order is prime.
derive: Conversely Lagrange shows a group of prime order has only trivial subgroups.

drafts.canonical_statement: The alternating group on a finite set with at least 5 elements is simple.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>5</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="alternating_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show that a nontrivial normal subgroup contains a 3-cycle, and that 3-cycles are conjugate and generate.
sketch_steps: translate: The alternating group is generated by 3-cycles.
derive: With at least 5 points all 3-cycles are conjugate in the alternating group.
setup: Let N be a nontrivial normal subgroup and take a non-identity element.
case_split: According to its cycle type, form commutators with suitable elements.
derive: These commutators lie in N and lead to a 3-cycle in N.
conclude: Then N contains all 3-cycles, so it is the whole group.

drafts.canonical_statement: The symmetric group on a finite set is generated by the transpositions.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="generated_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="suchthat"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="transposition"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the number of points moved, peeling off one transposition.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on the number of points moved by σ.
setup: If σ(x) ≠ x, let τ swap x and σ(x).
derive: τσ fixes x and every point fixed by σ, so it moves fewer points.
conclude: Then σ = τ(τσ) is a product of transpositions.

drafts.canonical_statement: A transposition has sign -1, and a cycle of length k has sign (-1)^(k-1).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="transposition"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="permutation_sign"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>-1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cycle_permutation"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="permutation_sign"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>-1</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cycle_length"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Write a k-cycle as a product of k-1 transpositions.
sketch_steps: derive: A transposition changes the parity of the number of inversions, so its sign is -1.
translate: A k-cycle is a product of k-1 transpositions.
conclude: Multiplicativity of the sign gives (-1)^(k-1).

drafts.canonical_statement: The alternating group on a finite set with n ≥ 2 elements is a normal subgroup of index 2 and satisfies 2·|A_n| = n!.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="alternating_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="alternating_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="alternating_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Realize the alternating group as the kernel of the surjective sign map.
sketch_steps: translate: The alternating group is the kernel of the sign homomorphism.
derive: A transposition exists, so the sign is surjective.
apply_theorem: The first isomorphism theorem gives index 2.
conclude: Lagrange and |Sym(X)| = n! give 2|A(X)| = n!.

drafts.canonical_statement: The alternating group on a finite set is generated by the 3-cycles.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="generated_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="suchthat"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="three_cycle"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="alternating_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Pair up transpositions in an even permutation and rewrite each pair as 3-cycles.
sketch_steps: derive: A 3-cycle is a product of two transpositions, so it is even.
translate: An even permutation is a product of an even number of transpositions.
case_split: Two transpositions are equal, share one point, or are disjoint.
derive: In each case their product is a product of 3-cycles.
conclude: The 3-cycles generate the alternating group.

drafts.canonical_statement: If normal subgroups H and K of a group G satisfy H ∩ K = 1 and HK = G, then G is isomorphic to H × K.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_join"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="isomorphic_groups"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="direct_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use commuting of H and K to make multiplication a homomorphism and check bijectivity.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Normal subgroups with trivial intersection commute elementwise.
construct: Define φ(h, k) = hk.
derive: Commutativity makes φ a homomorphism.
derive: hk = 1 gives h = k⁻¹ in H ∩ K, so φ is injective.
derive: The subgroup generated by H and K equals HK, so φ is surjective.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a normal subgroup N and a subgroup H of G satisfy N ∩ H = 1 and NH = G, then G is isomorphic to the semidirect product of N by H for the conjugation action φ(h)(n) = hnh⁻¹.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_join"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="isomorphic_groups"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="semidirect_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show that (n, h) ↦ nh is a bijective homomorphism from the semidirect product.
sketch_steps: construct: Let φ(h) be conjugation by h on N and form the semidirect product.
derive: The map (n, h) ↦ nh is a homomorphism because nhn'h' = n(hn'h⁻¹)hh'.
derive: nh = 1 forces n = h⁻¹ in N ∩ H, so the map is injective.
derive: The subgroup generated by N and H is NH, so the map is surjective.

drafts.canonical_statement: Structure theorem: every finite abelian group is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of cyclic groups Z/p_i^(e_i) with each p_i prime.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="abelian_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="isomorphic_groups"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_power_cyclic_sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Decompose into p-primary parts, then split off a cyclic subgroup of maximal order.
sketch_steps: translate: G is the direct sum of its p-primary components.
setup: Fix a finite abelian p-group A and choose x of maximal order.
derive: The cyclic subgroup generated by x is a direct summand of A.
induction: Apply induction to the complement.
conclude: G is a direct sum of cyclic groups of prime power order.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a normal subgroup N of a group G, G is solvable if and only if both N and G/N are solvable.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="quotient_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare derived series of G, N and G/N.
sketch_steps: derive: The derived series of N is contained in that of G.
derive: The derived series of G/N is the image of that of G.
setup: Conversely assume the k-th derived subgroup of G/N and the l-th derived subgroup of N are trivial.
derive: Then G^(k) ≤ N, so G^(k+l) ≤ N^(l) = 1.
conclude: G is solvable exactly when both N and G/N are.

drafts.canonical_statement: The symmetric group S_n is not solvable for n ≥ 5.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>5</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show every derived subgroup contains all 3-cycles, using five distinct points.
sketch_steps: derive: With five points every 3-cycle is a commutator of two 3-cycles.
induction: Each term of the derived series contains all 3-cycles.
conclude: The derived series never becomes trivial, so S_n is not solvable.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every finite p-group is nilpotent.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="p_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the order, dividing by the nontrivial center.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on |G|, the trivial group being nilpotent.
apply_theorem: A nontrivial p-group has a nontrivial center.
derive: G/Z(G) is a smaller p-group, hence nilpotent.
conclude: A central extension of a nilpotent group is nilpotent.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nilpotent group is solvable, and a nontrivial nilpotent group has nontrivial center.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the upper central series, whose factors are abelian.
sketch_steps: setup: Take the upper central series ending at G.
derive: Its factors are central in the quotients, hence abelian.
conclude: This abelian series shows G is solvable.
contradiction: If Z(G) were trivial, every term of the series would be trivial, contradicting that the series reaches a nontrivial G.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every nontrivial finite group G has a normal subgroup N such that G/N is simple. This is the step used to build a composition series.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take a maximal proper normal subgroup and apply the correspondence theorem.
sketch_steps: construct: Finiteness gives a maximal element N among proper normal subgroups.
derive: G/N is nontrivial because N is proper.
setup: Let K be a normal subgroup of G/N with preimage L.
derive: L is a normal subgroup of G containing N.
case_split: If L = G then K = G/N; otherwise maximality gives L = N and K is trivial.
conclude: G/N is simple.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take a shortest nontrivial linear relation and eliminate one term using f minus a scalar.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose a nontrivial linear relation among the eigenvectors exists and choose one with the fewest terms.
derive: Apply f and subtract μ_i times the relation to remove the i-th term.
derive: The surviving coefficients are multiplied by μ_j - μ_i, which are nonzero by distinctness.
contradiction: This is a shorter nontrivial relation, contradicting minimality.

contradiction: If μ = 0 then x = 0, contrary to the hypothesis.
conclude: Multiply by μ⁻¹ to obtain g x = μ⁻¹ x.

drafts.canonical_statement: A linear endomorphism f has eigenvalue 0 if and only if f is not injective.

drafts.proof_strategy: Identify the eigenspace for 0 with the kernel.
sketch_steps: translate: The eigenspace of f for 0 equals ker f.
apply_theorem: A linear map is injective exactly when its kernel is zero.
conclude: Hence eigenvalue 0 exists exactly when f is not injective.

sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.
apply_theorem: An independent family of size equal to the dimension spans the space.
construct: Build the basis from the family v.
conclude: Each basis vector satisfies f b_i = μ_i b_i.

drafts.proof_strategy: Extract a basis from the spanning set of eigenvectors, and conversely span by the basis.
sketch_steps: setup: Let S be the set of vectors x with f x = a x for some scalar a.
translate: The sum of the eigenspaces is the span of S.
apply_theorem: A spanning set of a vector space contains a basis.
construct: Choose for each basis vector a scalar a with f b = a b.
derive: Conversely each basis vector lies in an eigenspace, so the sum contains the span of the basis.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a linear endomorphism satisfies f ∘ f = f, then the sum of its eigenspaces for 1 and 0 is the whole space.

drafts.proof_strategy: Decompose x as f x plus x - f x.
sketch_steps: setup: Write x = f x + (x - f x).
derive: f (f x) = f x shows that f x lies in the eigenspace for 1.
derive: f (x - f x) = 0 shows that x - f x lies in the eigenspace for 0.
conclude: The sum of the two eigenspaces is the whole space.

drafts.canonical_statement: Over an algebraically closed field, if the minimal polynomial of a linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space is squarefree, then its eigenspaces span the space.

drafts.proof_strategy: Squarefree minimal polynomial implies semisimple, and semisimple over an algebraically closed field means eigenspaces span.
sketch_steps: translate: f is annihilated by the squarefree polynomial minpoly f.
apply_theorem: An endomorphism annihilated by a squarefree polynomial is semisimple.
apply_theorem: Over an algebraically closed field a semisimple endomorphism has generalized eigenspaces equal to eigenspaces.
conclude: Generalized eigenspaces span, so the eigenspaces span.

drafts.canonical_statement: A linear endomorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field has an eigenvalue.

drafts.proof_strategy: The characteristic polynomial has positive degree, so it has a root.
sketch_steps: derive: The characteristic polynomial of f has degree dim V, which is positive.
apply_theorem: A nonconstant polynomial over an algebraically closed field has a root.
conclude: A root of the characteristic polynomial is an eigenvalue.

drafts.canonical_statement: Cayley-Hamilton theorem: a square matrix over a commutative ring is annihilated by its characteristic polynomial.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the adjugate identity in the polynomial ring and compare coefficients.
sketch_steps: setup: Let B be the adjugate of XE - A over R[X].
derive: B (XE - A) = p_A(X) E holds by the adjugate identity.
translate: Expand B as a polynomial in X with matrix coefficients.
derive: Compare coefficients of X^k and multiply by powers of A.
conclude: The sum telescopes, giving p_A(A) = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the Bezout identity to f.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose a, b with a p + b q = 1 and evaluate at f.
derive: A vector killed by both p(f) and q(f) is zero.
derive: For x in ker (pq)(f), the two Bezout terms lie in ker q(f) and ker p(f).
derive: Both kernels are contained in ker (pq)(f) since polynomials in f commute.
conclude: The kernel of the product is the direct sum.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space over an algebraically closed field, the generalized eigenspaces span the whole space.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on dimension using the kernel-image decomposition of (f - μ)^k.
sketch_steps: setup: Induct on dim V; the case V = 0 is trivial.
apply_theorem: A nonzero space has an eigenvalue μ over an algebraically closed field.
derive: For large k, V is the direct sum of ker (f-μ)^k and im (f-μ)^k.
induction: Apply the hypothesis to f restricted to the invariant image, whose dimension is smaller.
conclude: Add the kernel part, which lies in the generalized eigenspace of μ.

drafts.canonical_statement: If x ≠ 0 and (f - μ)^k x = 0 for some natural number k, then μ is an eigenvalue of f.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="endomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fn_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="op_pow"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="smul"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="identity_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="eigenvalue_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Take the last nonzero vector in the chain x, (f-μ)x, ….
sketch_steps: setup: Take the least m with (f-μ)^m x = 0.
derive: Since x ≠ 0, m is at least 1.
construct: Let y = (f-μ)^(m-1) x, which is nonzero by minimality.
conclude: (f-μ) y = 0, so y is an eigenvector for μ.

drafts.canonical_statement: A linear endomorphism f of a nonzero finite-dimensional space over an algebraically closed field has an invariant subspace of codimension one.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="alg_closed_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="endomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="zero_subspace"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dim_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dim_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="invariant_subspace"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Take the kernel of an eigenvector of the dual map.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The dual map of f has an eigenvector φ on the nonzero dual space.
construct: Let W be the kernel of φ.
derive: Since φ is a nonzero functional, W has codimension one.
derive: For x in W, φ(f x) = μ φ(x) = 0, so W is invariant.
conclude: W is the required hyperplane.

drafts.canonical_statement: Fitting's lemma: for a linear endomorphism f of a finite-dimensional space V, for all sufficiently large n the space V is the direct sum of ker f^n and im f^n.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="endomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_complement"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="kernel"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="op_pow"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="range_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="op_pow"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use stabilization of kernels and images together with rank-nullity.
sketch_steps: derive: The chains ker f^n and im f^n stabilize from some N because V is finite-dimensional.
setup: Fix n ≥ N and take x in ker f^n ∩ im f^n, x = f^n y.
derive: Then y lies in ker f^(2n) = ker f^n, so x = 0.
apply_theorem: Rank-nullity gives dim ker f^n + dim im f^n = dim V.
conclude: The two subspaces are complementary.

drafts.canonical_statement: Jordan-Chevalley decomposition: a linear endomorphism f of a finite-dimensional space over a perfect field is a sum f = n + s with n nilpotent, s semisimple, and both n and s polynomials in f.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="perfect_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="endomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_op"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="semisimple_op"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Run Newton iteration on the separable radical of the minimal polynomial.
sketch_steps: setup: Let g be the squarefree radical of the minimal polynomial; g is separable because K is perfect.
derive: g(f) is nilpotent and g'(f) is invertible in the algebra generated by f.
apply_theorem: Newton iteration yields s in that algebra with g(s) = 0 and f - s nilpotent.
derive: Since g is squarefree, s is semisimple.
conclude: Put n = f - s.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every eigenvalue of a nilpotent linear endomorphism is zero.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="endomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_op"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="eigenvalue_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the k-th power to an eigenvector.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose k with f^k = 0 and an eigenvector x for μ.
derive: f^k x = μ^k x, so μ^k x = 0.
derive: Because x ≠ 0, μ^k = 0.
conclude: A field has no nonzero nilpotents, so μ = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nilpotent linear endomorphism f of an n-dimensional vector space satisfies f^n = 0.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="endomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_op"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="op_pow"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dim_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The characteristic polynomial of a nilpotent map is X^n, then apply Cayley-Hamilton.
sketch_steps: derive: The characteristic polynomial of a nilpotent f equals X^(dim V).
apply_theorem: By Cayley-Hamilton the characteristic polynomial annihilates f.
conclude: Therefore f^(dim V) = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: The trace of a nilpotent linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space is zero.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="endomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_op"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trace_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Read the trace from the characteristic polynomial X^n.
sketch_steps: derive: The characteristic polynomial of f is X^(dim V).
translate: The trace is minus the subleading coefficient of the characteristic polynomial.
conclude: That coefficient vanishes, so tr f = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality: in a real or complex inner product space, |⟨x,y⟩| ≤ ‖x‖‖y‖ for all vectors x and y.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="inner_product_space_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="abs"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="inner_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Project y onto x and use nonnegativity of the squared norm of the remainder.
sketch_steps: case_split: The case x = 0 is immediate.
construct: For x ≠ 0 set t = ⟨x,y⟩/‖x‖² and z = y - t x.
derive: ⟨x,z⟩ = 0, so ‖y‖² = |t|²‖x‖² + ‖z‖².
derive: Hence |⟨x,y⟩|²/‖x‖² ≤ ‖y‖².
conclude: Multiply by ‖x‖² and take square roots.

drafts.canonical_statement: For nonzero vectors x and y in an inner product space, |⟨x,y⟩| = ‖x‖‖y‖ if and only if y = r x for some nonzero scalar r.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="inner_product_space_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="abs"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="inner_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="smul"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Analyze the remainder term in the Cauchy-Schwarz proof.
sketch_steps: construct: Set t = ⟨x,y⟩/‖x‖² and z = y - t x.
derive: ‖y‖² = |t|²‖x‖² + ‖z‖² by orthogonality.
translate: Equality in Cauchy-Schwarz is equivalent to z = 0.
derive: Since y ≠ 0, the scalar t is nonzero.
derive: Conversely y = r x gives |⟨x,y⟩| = |r|‖x‖² = ‖x‖‖y‖.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: In an inner product space, ‖x + y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ for all vectors x and y.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="inner_product_space_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Expand the squared norm and bound the cross term by Cauchy-Schwarz.
sketch_steps: derive: ‖x+y‖² = ‖x‖² + 2 Re⟨x,y⟩ + ‖y‖².
apply_theorem: Cauchy-Schwarz gives Re⟨x,y⟩ ≤ ‖x‖‖y‖.
conclude: So ‖x+y‖² ≤ (‖x‖+‖y‖)², and square roots give the claim.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a real inner product space, ‖x+y‖² = ‖x‖² + ‖y‖² if and only if ⟨x,y⟩ = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Expand the squared norm by bilinearity.
sketch_steps: derive: ‖x+y‖² = ‖x‖² + 2⟨x,y⟩ + ‖y‖² in a real inner product space.
conclude: The stated identity is equivalent to ⟨x,y⟩ = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a real inner product space, ⟨x,y⟩ = (‖x+y‖² - ‖x-y‖²)/4.

drafts.proof_strategy: Subtract the two expansions of the squared norms.
sketch_steps: derive: Expand ‖x+y‖² and ‖x-y‖² by bilinearity.
conclude: Their difference is 4⟨x,y⟩.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compute the real and imaginary parts of the inner product separately.
sketch_steps: derive: ‖x+y‖² - ‖x-y‖² equals 4 Re⟨x,y⟩.
derive: Replacing y by i y gives ‖x-iy‖² - ‖x+iy‖² = 4 Im⟨x,y⟩.
conclude: Combine using ⟨x,y⟩ = Re⟨x,y⟩ + i Im⟨x,y⟩.

drafts.canonical_statement: A family of nonzero pairwise orthogonal vectors in an inner product space is linearly independent.

drafts.proof_strategy: Pair a vanishing linear combination with each v_j.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose a finite combination Σ a_i v_i vanishes.
derive: Taking the inner product with v_j leaves a_j ‖v_j‖² = 0.
conclude: Since v_j ≠ 0, every a_j = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a linearly independent family v_1,…,v_n in an inner product space there is an orthonormal family u_1,…,u_n such that for each k the first k vectors of u and of v span the same subspace.

drafts.proof_strategy: Subtract projections onto earlier vectors and normalize inductively.
sketch_steps: construct: Define w_k = v_k - Σ_{j<k} ⟨u_j,v_k⟩ u_j and u_k = w_k/‖w_k‖.
derive: Independence gives w_k ≠ 0, so u_k is defined.
derive: A direct computation shows ⟨u_j,w_k⟩ = 0 for j < k.
induction: The spans of the first k vectors coincide by induction on k.
conclude: u is orthonormal with the required span property.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every orthonormal subset of a finite-dimensional inner product space extends to an orthonormal basis.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_inner_product_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="orthonormal_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="family_extends_to_onb"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Add an orthonormal basis of the orthogonal complement of the span.
sketch_steps: setup: Let S be the span of v.
apply_theorem: The finite-dimensional space S^⊥ has an orthonormal basis w.
derive: v ∪ w is orthonormal because w is orthogonal to S.
derive: E = S ⊕ S^⊥ shows that v ∪ w spans E.
conclude: v ∪ w is an orthonormal basis containing v.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a subspace S of a finite-dimensional inner product space, the orthogonal complement of S^⊥ equals S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_inner_product_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subspace_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="orthogonal_complement"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="orthogonal_complement"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare dimensions using the inclusion S ⊆ S^⊥⊥.
sketch_steps: derive: Each element of S is orthogonal to S^⊥, so S ⊆ (S^⊥)^⊥.
apply_theorem: dim T + dim T^⊥ = dim E for each subspace T.
derive: Applying this twice gives dim (S^⊥)^⊥ = dim S.
conclude: The inclusion is an equality.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a subspace S of a finite-dimensional inner product space E, E is the direct sum of S and S^⊥, and dim S + dim S^⊥ = dim E.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_inner_product_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subspace_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_complement"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="orthogonal_complement"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dim_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dim_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="orthogonal_complement"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dim_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use an orthonormal basis of S to construct the orthogonal projection.
sketch_steps: derive: S ∩ S^⊥ = 0 because ⟨x,x⟩ = 0 forces x = 0.
construct: With an orthonormal basis (e_i) of S set p = Σ ⟨e_i,x⟩ e_i.
derive: x - p is orthogonal to each e_i, so x - p ∈ S^⊥.
derive: Hence E = S + S^⊥.
conclude: The dimension formula for direct sums gives the equality.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a subspace S of a finite-dimensional inner product space and a point x, the orthogonal projection of x onto S minimizes the distance from x among points of S.

drafts.proof_strategy: Split x - w into orthogonal parts and apply Pythagoras.
sketch_steps: setup: Let p be the orthogonal projection of x and write x - w = (x - p) + (p - w).
derive: x - p lies in S^⊥ and p - w lies in S, so they are orthogonal.
apply_theorem: Pythagoras gives ‖x-w‖² = ‖x-p‖² + ‖p-w‖².
conclude: Therefore ‖x-p‖ ≤ ‖x-w‖.

drafts.canonical_statement: If v ∈ S and x - v is orthogonal to every element of S, then v is the orthogonal projection of x onto S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fd_inner_product_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subspace_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="inner_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="orthogonal_projection"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The difference of two candidates lies in S ∩ S^⊥.
sketch_steps: setup: Let p be the projection, so x - p ∈ S^⊥.
derive: p - v = (x - v) - (x - p) lies in S^⊥ and in S.
conclude: S ∩ S^⊥ = 0 forces p = v.

drafts.proof_strategy: Verify the defining identity of the adjoint.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix x in E and y in G.
derive: ⟨A(Bx),y⟩ = ⟨Bx,A*y⟩ = ⟨x,B*A*y⟩.
conclude: Uniqueness of the adjoint gives (A∘B)* = B*∘A*.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a linear map T between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, the kernel of the adjoint T* equals the orthogonal complement of the image of T.

drafts.proof_strategy: Rewrite membership with the defining identity of the adjoint.
sketch_steps: derive: ⟨Tw,y⟩ = ⟨w,T*y⟩ for all w and y.
translate: y ∈ (im T)^⊥ means the left side vanishes for all w.
apply_theorem: Nondegeneracy says the right side vanishes for all w exactly when T*y = 0.
conclude: Thus ker T* = (im T)^⊥.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every eigenvalue μ of a self-adjoint linear endomorphism is real, that is, the conjugate of μ equals μ.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compare ⟨Tx,x⟩ and ⟨x,Tx⟩ on an eigenvector.
sketch_steps: setup: Pick an eigenvector x for μ.
derive: ⟨Tx,x⟩ is the conjugate of μ times ‖x‖², and ⟨x,Tx⟩ is μ‖x‖².
derive: Self-adjointness makes these two values equal.
conclude: Since ‖x‖² ≠ 0, μ equals its conjugate.

sketch_steps: case_split: The case x = 0 or y = 0 is immediate.
apply_theorem: Otherwise μ and ν are eigenvalues of T, hence real.
derive: ⟨Tx,y⟩ = μ⟨x,y⟩ and ⟨x,Ty⟩ = ν⟨x,y⟩.
derive: Self-adjointness gives (μ-ν)⟨x,y⟩ = 0.
conclude: Since μ ≠ ν, ⟨x,y⟩ = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Find one eigenvector by maximizing the Rayleigh quotient, then induct on the orthogonal complement.
sketch_steps: setup: Induct on dim E.
apply_theorem: A maximizer of ⟨Tx,x⟩ on the unit sphere is an eigenvector with real eigenvalue.
derive: The orthogonal complement of this eigenvector is T-invariant.
induction: The restriction of T to the complement is self-adjoint, so it has an orthonormal eigenbasis.
conclude: Adding the normalized eigenvector gives the required basis.

drafts.proof_strategy: Move T across the inner product and use commutativity.
sketch_steps: derive: ‖Tx‖² = ⟨x,T*Tx⟩ by the adjoint identity.
derive: ‖T*x‖² = ⟨x,TT*x⟩ in the same way.
conclude: Normality equates the two, and norms are nonnegative.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a real square matrix A satisfies AᵀA = E, then (Ax)·(Ay) = x·y for all vectors x and y.

sketch_steps: derive: (Ax)·(Ay) = x·(Aᵀ(Ay)).
derive: Aᵀ(Ay) = (AᵀA)y = y.
conclude: The value is x·y.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a real square matrix A satisfies AᵀA = E, then det A = 1 or det A = -1.

sketch_steps: derive: det(Aᵀ) det A = det E = 1.
derive: det(Aᵀ) = det A, so (det A)² = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: A real symmetric matrix is positive definite if and only if all of its eigenvalues are positive.

drafts.proof_strategy: Diagonalize A orthogonally and read the quadratic form in the new coordinates.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Write A = U D Uᵀ with U orthogonal and D diagonal.
translate: With y = Uᵀ x, the quadratic form is Σ d_i y_i².
derive: x ≠ 0 is equivalent to y ≠ 0 because U is invertible.
derive: Positive d_i make the form positive on nonzero vectors.
derive: Taking y to be a standard basis vector shows that positive definiteness forces d_i > 0.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

conclude: Adding x gives an orthogonal basis of V.

drafts.proof_strategy: Normalize an orthogonal basis for existence, and identify the positive count with a basis-free maximum dimension.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: A symmetric bilinear form has an orthogonal basis.
construct: Rescale each basis vector by the inverse square root of |q(v_i)| when nonzero.
translate: Let p be the maximal dimension of a subspace on which q is positive definite.
derive: A positive definite subspace meets the span of nonpositive coefficients only in 0, so its dimension is at most the positive count.
derive: The span of the positive coefficient vectors attains this bound, so the count equals p.
derive: Apply the same argument to -q for the negative count.
conclude: Both counts depend only on q.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a subspace W of a finite-dimensional vector space V with annihilator W⁰ in the dual space, dim W + dim W⁰ = dim V.

drafts.proof_strategy: Extend a basis of W and read the annihilator in the dual basis.
sketch_steps: construct: Extend a basis of W to a basis of V and take the dual basis.
translate: φ = Σ a_i φ_i vanishes on W exactly when a_1 = … = a_m = 0.
derive: The functionals φ_{m+1},…,φ_n form a basis of W⁰.
conclude: dim W⁰ = dim V - dim W.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finite-dimensional vector space V, the canonical evaluation map from V to its double dual, x ↦ (φ ↦ φ(x)), is bijective.

drafts.proof_strategy: Prove injectivity using a dual basis and compare dimensions.
sketch_steps: derive: For x ≠ 0, extending x to a basis gives a functional φ with φ(x) ≠ 0.
derive: So the evaluation map is injective.
apply_theorem: dim V** = dim V* = dim V.
conclude: An injective linear map between spaces of equal finite dimension is bijective.
