drafts.proof_strategy: Pick an element of I outside P and apply the prime condition to its products with J.
sketch_steps: case_split: Assume I is not contained in P and take a in I outside P.
derive: For b in J, ab lies in IJ and hence in P.
derive: Primality of P forces b into P.
conclude: Thus J is contained in P.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every finite integral domain is a field.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Multiplication by a nonzero element is injective, hence surjective on a finite set.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a nonzero element a of R.
derive: Cancellation makes x ↦ ax injective.
derive: Finiteness makes the map surjective.
conclude: Some b satisfies ab = 1, so a is a unit.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a commutative ring, the sum of a unit and a nilpotent element is a unit.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Factor out u and invert 1 - m by the finite geometric series.
sketch_steps: setup: Put m = -u⁻¹n, which is nilpotent by commutativity.
derive: Then u + n = u(1 - m).
construct: If m^k = 0, the sum 1 + m + ... + m^(k-1) inverts 1 - m.
conclude: So u + n is a product of units.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every prime element of an integral domain is irreducible.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use primality on a factorization and cancel p.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose p = ab.
derive: Primality gives p | a or p | b.
case_split: If a = pc, then p = pcb.
derive: Cancelling p shows b is a unit.
conclude: The other case is symmetric, so p is irreducible.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every irreducible element of a principal ideal domain is prime.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="principal_ideal_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Generate the ideal (p, a) by one element and extract a Bezout identity.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose p divides ab but not a.
construct: Write the ideal (p, a) as (d).
derive: Since d divides p and p does not divide a, irreducibility makes d a unit.
derive: Hence 1 = px + ay.
conclude: Multiplying by b shows p divides b.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a unique factorization domain, an element is irreducible if and only if it is prime.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unique_factorization_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare the factorizations of ab and pc using uniqueness.
sketch_steps: derive: Prime elements are irreducible in any domain.
setup: Let p be irreducible with p | ab, and write ab = pc.
case_split: The case a = 0 or b = 0 is immediate.
derive: Uniqueness of factorization makes p an associate of an irreducible factor of a or b.
conclude: So p divides a or b.

drafts.canonical_statement: In the ring Z[√-5], the element 2 is irreducible but not prime.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="int_adjoin_sqrt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>-5</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="int_adjoin_sqrt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>-5</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the multiplicative norm for irreducibility and the factorization of 6 for non-primality.
sketch_steps: setup: Use the multiplicative norm N(a + b√-5) = a² + 5b².
derive: A factorization of 2 gives norms multiplying to 4.
derive: The equation a² + 5b² = 2 has no integer solution, so one factor has norm 1 and is a unit.
derive: The element 2 divides (1 + √-5)(1 - √-5) = 6.
contradiction: Neither factor is divisible by 2 because its √-5 coefficient is odd.
conclude: So 2 is irreducible but not prime.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every Euclidean domain is a principal ideal domain.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="euclidean_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="principal_ideal_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Generate the ideal by a nonzero element of minimal Euclidean size.
sketch_steps: setup: Let I be a nonzero ideal.
construct: Pick a nonzero d in I of minimal Euclidean size.
derive: For x in I, divide to get x = dq + r with r in I.
contradiction: A nonzero r would have smaller size than d.
conclude: So r = 0 and I = (d).

drafts.canonical_statement: Every principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="principal_ideal_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unique_factorization_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Get existence from the ascending chain condition and uniqueness from irreducible elements being prime.
sketch_steps: derive: Every ascending chain of principal ideals stabilizes because its union is principal.
derive: A nonzero non-unit therefore factors into irreducibles in finitely many steps.
apply_theorem: Irreducible elements of a principal ideal domain are prime.
induction: Cancel prime factors one at a time to compare two factorizations.
conclude: The factorization is unique up to order and associates.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every nonzero prime ideal of a principal ideal domain is maximal.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="principal_ideal_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="zero_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Write P = (p), factor p through any larger ideal, and use primality with cancellation.
sketch_steps: setup: Write P = (p) with p nonzero and take (a) containing P.
derive: Then p = ab for some b.
case_split: Primality puts a or b in P.
derive: If a is in P then (a) = P.
derive: If b = pc then cancelling p gives ac = 1, so (a) = R.
conclude: Hence P is maximal.

drafts.canonical_statement: Gauss's theorem. If R is a unique factorization domain, then the polynomial ring R[X] is also a unique factorization domain.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unique_factorization_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unique_factorization_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce to the Euclidean ring K[X] and to R through contents and Gauss's lemma.
sketch_steps: setup: Let K be the field of fractions of R.
derive: Write a polynomial as its content times a primitive polynomial.
apply_theorem: Factor the primitive part in the unique factorization domain K[X].
apply_theorem: Gauss's lemma brings the factorization back to R[X].
conclude: Uniqueness in R and K[X] gives uniqueness in R[X].

drafts.canonical_statement: For a polynomial f and a monic polynomial g over a nontrivial commutative ring, there are polynomials q and r with f = gq + r and deg r < deg g.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nontrivial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="monic_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="lt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the degree of f and remove the leading term using the monic divisor.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on the degree of f.
case_split: If deg f < deg g, take q = 0 and r = f.
derive: Otherwise subtract aX^(n-m)g, which lowers the degree because g is monic.
conclude: Add aX^(n-m) to the quotient from the induction hypothesis.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a polynomial f over a commutative ring and an element a, there is a polynomial q with f = (X - a)q + f(a).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_var"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_const"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_const"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Divide by the monic polynomial X - a and substitute X = a.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Divide f by the monic polynomial X - a.
derive: The remainder r has degree below 1, so it is a constant.
conclude: Substituting X = a shows r = f(a).

drafts.canonical_statement: Factor theorem. For a polynomial f over a commutative ring and an element a, X - a divides f if and only if f(a) = 0.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dvd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_var"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_const"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Substitute in one direction and use the remainder theorem in the other.
sketch_steps: derive: If f = (X - a)g, substituting a gives f(a) = 0.
apply_theorem: The remainder theorem gives f = (X - a)q + f(a).
conclude: If f(a) = 0 this says X - a divides f.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nonzero polynomial over an integral domain has at most as many distinct roots as its degree.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Peel off one root by the factor theorem and use that a domain has no zero divisors.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on the degree of f.
apply_theorem: If a is a root, the factor theorem gives f = (X - a)g.
derive: For another root b, 0 = (b - a)g(b), so g(b) = 0.
conclude: The remaining roots are roots of g, so the bound follows.

drafts.canonical_statement: Gauss's lemma. Over a GCD domain, which includes every unique factorization domain, the product of two primitive polynomials is primitive.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="gcd_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="primitive_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="primitive_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="primitive_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce modulo a prime divisor of the content and use that the reduced polynomial ring is a domain.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose fg is not primitive, and take a prime p dividing all its coefficients.
translate: Reduce coefficients modulo p.
derive: The polynomial ring over the domain R/(p) is a domain.
derive: The image of fg vanishes, so the image of f or g vanishes.
contradiction: Then p divides every coefficient of f or g.
conclude: The general GCD case follows by multiplicativity of content.

drafts.canonical_statement: A primitive polynomial with integer coefficients is irreducible in Z[X] if and only if it is irreducible in Q[X].
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Z"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="primitive_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Z"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Clear denominators to primitive factors and apply Gauss's lemma.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose f = gh in Q[X] with both factors of positive degree.
construct: Rescale g and h to primitive integer polynomials g₀ and h₀, so f = c g₀ h₀.
apply_theorem: Gauss's lemma makes g₀h₀ primitive.
derive: Since f is primitive, c = ±1, which factors f in Z[X].
derive: Conversely, non-unit factors of primitive f in Z[X] are nonconstant.
conclude: So such a factorization remains proper in Q[X].

drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce modulo P, where the polynomial becomes a monomial, and deduce that both constant terms lie in P.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose f = gh with non-units g and h.
derive: Primitivity forces both factors to have positive degree.
translate: Modulo P the image of f is a nonzero monomial cXⁿ.
derive: Over the fraction field of R/P, the images of g and h are monomials of positive degree.
derive: Hence the constant terms of g and h both lie in P.
contradiction: The constant term of f then lies in P².

drafts.canonical_statement: Let f in Z[X] be monic of positive degree and p a prime. If p divides every non-leading coefficient and p² does not divide the constant term, then f is irreducible in Q[X].

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Eisenstein at the ideal (p), then transfer irreducibility to Q[X] by Gauss.
sketch_steps: derive: A monic polynomial is primitive.
translate: The divisibility conditions say the coefficients lie in (p) and the constant term is not in (p²).
apply_theorem: Eisenstein's criterion gives irreducibility in Z[X].
apply_theorem: Gauss's lemma transfers irreducibility to Q[X].

drafts.canonical_statement: Let φ from R to S be a ring homomorphism between integral domains and f in R[X] monic. If the polynomial obtained by applying φ to the coefficients is irreducible in S[X], then f is irreducible in R[X].

drafts.proof_strategy: Use that a monic factorization preserves degrees under reduction.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose f = gh.
derive: The leading coefficients of g and h multiply to 1, so they are units.
derive: Hence φ preserves the degrees of g and h.
apply_theorem: Irreducibility of φ(f) makes one image a unit of degree 0.
conclude: The corresponding factor has degree 0 and unit leading coefficient, so it is a unit.

drafts.canonical_statement: A polynomial of degree 2 or 3 over a field K is irreducible if and only if it has no root in K.

drafts.proof_strategy: Link roots to linear factors and use the small degree to force a linear factor.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: A root a gives f = (X - a)g by the factor theorem.
derive: Since deg g ≥ 1, f is reducible.
setup: Conversely suppose f = gh with non-units g and h.
derive: Degrees are at least 1 and sum to at most 3, so one factor is linear.
conclude: A linear factor over a field has a root, which is a root of f.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a polynomial f over a field K, the quotient K[X]/(f) is a field if and only if f is irreducible.

drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce to maximality of (f) in the principal ideal domain K[X], treating f = 0 separately.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The quotient is a field exactly when (f) is maximal.
case_split: If f = 0, both sides fail because K[X] is not a field and 0 is not irreducible.
derive: If f ≠ 0 and (f) is maximal, then (f) is prime, so f is prime and irreducible.
derive: If f is irreducible and (f) ⊆ (g), then g is a unit or an associate of f.
conclude: Hence (f) is maximal exactly when f is irreducible.

drafts.canonical_statement: The characteristic of an integral domain is either zero or a prime number.

drafts.proof_strategy: Factor the characteristic and use the absence of zero divisors.
sketch_steps: setup: Assume p ≠ 0; since 1 ≠ 0, also p ≠ 1.
case_split: Suppose p = ab with 1 < a, b < p.
derive: Then (a·1)(b·1) = 0 in R.
contradiction: One factor vanishes, against minimality of p.
conclude: So p is prime.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a commutative ring of prime characteristic p, one has (x + y)^p = x^p + y^p.

drafts.proof_strategy: Expand by the binomial theorem and kill the middle binomial coefficients.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Expand (x + y)^p by the binomial theorem.
derive: For 0 < k < p, the prime p divides the binomial coefficient C(p, k).
conclude: In characteristic p only x^p and y^p remain.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a reduced commutative ring of prime characteristic p, the Frobenius map is injective, that is, x^p = y^p implies x = y.

drafts.proof_strategy: Turn equal p-th powers into nilpotence of the difference.
sketch_steps: derive: In characteristic p, (x - y)^p = x^p - y^p.
translate: The hypothesis gives (x - y)^p = 0, so x - y is nilpotent.
conclude: Reducedness gives x = y.

sketch_steps: translate: An element of K is a class of a pair (a, b) with b nonzero.

derive: The cross-multiplication relation shows h is well defined.
derive: Fraction arithmetic shows h is a ring homomorphism.
conclude: Any extension must satisfy the same formula, so it is unique.

drafts.canonical_statement: The nilradical of a commutative ring, that is, the set of its nilpotent elements, equals the intersection of all prime ideals.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilradical_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The easy inclusion uses primality; the other builds a prime ideal avoiding the powers of x by Zorn's lemma.
sketch_steps: derive: If x^n = 0, then x lies in every prime ideal.
setup: Conversely, let x be non-nilpotent.
apply_theorem: Zorn's lemma gives an ideal P maximal among those missing all powers of x.
derive: If a, b are outside P, then P + (a) and P + (b) contain powers of x.
contradiction: If ab were in P, a power of x would lie in P.
conclude: So P is a prime ideal not containing x.

drafts.canonical_statement: An element x lies in the Jacobson radical of a commutative ring if and only if xy + 1 is a unit for every y.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="jacobson_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Put a non-unit into a maximal ideal for one direction and use M + (x) = R for the other.
sketch_steps: setup: Assume x is in every maximal ideal.
contradiction: A non-unit xy + 1 lies in a maximal ideal containing x, which would contain 1.
setup: Conversely, suppose x is not in a maximal ideal M.
derive: Then M + (x) = R, so m + xz = 1 with m in M.
conclude: With y = -z, xy + 1 = m is not a unit.

drafts.canonical_statement: Nakayama's lemma. If an ideal I of a commutative ring R lies in the Jacobson radical and a finitely generated submodule N satisfies N ⊆ IN, then N = 0.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="submodule_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_submodule"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="jacobson_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_smul_submodule"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="zero_submodule"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Take a minimal generating set and eliminate one generator using that 1 - a is a unit.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose N ≠ 0 and choose a generating set of minimal size.
derive: Since N ⊆ IN, the last generator is an I-combination of all generators.
derive: Moving terms gives (1 - a) uₙ as a combination of the others.
apply_theorem: The element 1 - a is a unit because a lies in the Jacobson radical.
contradiction: Then uₙ is redundant, against minimality.

drafts.canonical_statement: The only idempotents of an integral domain are 0 and 1.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_domain"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="or"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Factor e² - e and use that a domain has no zero divisors.
sketch_steps: derive: The hypothesis gives e(e - 1) = 0.
conclude: With no zero divisors, e = 0 or e = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an idempotent e of a commutative ring, one has (e) + (1 - e) = R and (e) ∩ (1 - e) = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use 1 = e + (1 - e) and e(1 - e) = 0.
sketch_steps: derive: The identity 1 = e + (1 - e) shows the sum is R.
setup: Take x = ea = (1 - e)b in the intersection.
derive: Idempotence gives ex = x.
conclude: Also ex = e(1 - e)b = 0, so x = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: A square matrix A over a commutative ring R is a unit of the matrix ring if and only if det A is a unit of R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use multiplicativity of the determinant and the adjugate formula.
sketch_steps: derive: AB = E gives det A · det B = 1.
apply_theorem: The adjugate satisfies A adj A = adj A A = (det A) E.
conclude: If det A is a unit, then (det A)⁻¹ adj A inverts A.

drafts.canonical_statement: Over a nontrivial commutative ring, a matrix ring with at least two distinct indices contains a nonzero matrix A with A² = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Exhibit an off-diagonal matrix unit.
sketch_steps: construct: Take the matrix unit E_ij with i ≠ j.
derive: It is nonzero because 1 ≠ 0 in R.
conclude: The product rule for matrix units gives E_ij² = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: A commutative ring is Noetherian if and only if every ideal is finitely generated.

drafts.proof_strategy: Build a strict chain from a non-finitely-generated ideal, and conversely use generators of the union.
sketch_steps: contradiction: A non-finitely-generated ideal gives an infinite strict chain of finitely generated subideals.
setup: Conversely assume every ideal is finitely generated and take an ascending chain.
derive: The union is an ideal with finitely many generators.
derive: All generators appear at some stage of the chain.
conclude: The chain stabilizes there.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take the union, which is finitely generated, and locate its generators.
sketch_steps: derive: The union I of the chain is an ideal.
apply_theorem: Since R is Noetherian, I is finitely generated.
derive: The generators all lie in some I_N, so I = I_N.
conclude: For m ≥ N, I_N ⊆ I_m ⊆ I = I_N.

drafts.canonical_statement: Hilbert's basis theorem. If R is a Noetherian ring, then the polynomial ring R[X] is Noetherian.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Choose generators of minimal degree and use finite generation of the ideal of leading coefficients.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose an ideal I of R[X] is not finitely generated.
construct: Pick f_{k+1} of minimal degree in I outside (f_1, ..., f_k).
apply_theorem: The ideal of leading coefficients of the f_i is finitely generated.
derive: So some leading coefficient a_{k+1} is an R-combination of the earlier ones.
contradiction: Subtracting the matching combination gives an element of smaller degree outside (f_1, ..., f_k).

drafts.canonical_statement: In a topological space, the intersection of a finite family of open sets is open.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="open_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fn_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="open_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="family_inter"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the finite index set using the binary intersection axiom.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix the finite index set s and the open sets U_i.
induction: The empty intersection is X, which is open.
derive: Adding one index intersects the previous open set with one more open set.
conclude: The binary intersection axiom keeps the result open.

drafts.canonical_statement: A subset S of a topological space is open if and only if every point of S lies in an open set contained in S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="open_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="open_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Write S as the union of the local open sets.
sketch_steps: case_split: Prove the two implications separately.
derive: If S is open, take U = S for each point.
construct: Otherwise pick U_x for each x in S and form their union.
conclude: The union equals S and is open.

drafts.canonical_statement: A subset C of a metric space is closed if and only if the limit of every convergent sequence of points of C belongs to C.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="metric_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closed_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_tends_to"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the open complement in one direction and balls of radius 1/(n+1) in the other.
sketch_steps: case_split: Prove the two implications separately.
contradiction: A limit outside C would have an open neighborhood missing C.
construct: For a closure point a, choose a_n in C within distance 1/(n+1) of a.
derive: The sequence converges to a, so a lies in C.
conclude: The closure of C equals C, so C is closed.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a closed set C contains S, then C contains the closure of S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closed_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the definition of closure as the intersection of closed supersets.
sketch_steps: translate: The closure of S is the intersection of all closed supersets of S.
derive: C is one member of this family.
conclude: The intersection is contained in C.

drafts.canonical_statement: A point x lies in the closure of S if and only if every open set containing x meets S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="open_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="emptyset"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Prove both contrapositives using the complement of a separating set.
sketch_steps: translate: Work with contrapositives of both implications.
derive: An open U missing S gives the closed superset U^c excluding x.
derive: A closed superset C excluding x gives the open set C^c missing S.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: The closure of a union of two subsets equals the union of their closures.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="union"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="union"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use monotonicity for one inclusion and minimality of the closure for the other.
sketch_steps: derive: Monotonicity gives cl(S) ∪ cl(T) ⊆ cl(S ∪ T).
derive: cl(S) ∪ cl(T) is a closed set containing S ∪ T.
apply_theorem: Minimality of the closure gives the reverse inclusion.
conclude: Both inclusions yield equality.

drafts.canonical_statement: The interior of the complement of S equals the complement of the closure of S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="interior_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="setdiff"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="setdiff"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Dualize the definitions of interior and closure through complements.
sketch_steps: translate: Open subsets of S^c correspond to closed supersets of S by complement.
derive: The complement of the union of the former is the intersection of the latter.
conclude: Hence int(S^c) is the complement of cl(S).

drafts.canonical_statement: A subset S is closed if and only if its closure equals S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closed_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Combine minimality of the closure with the fact that closures are closed.
sketch_steps: derive: If S is closed, minimality gives cl(S) ⊆ S.
derive: S ⊆ cl(S) always holds, so they are equal.
conclude: Conversely S = cl(S) is closed because closures are closed.

drafts.canonical_statement: The boundary of S equals the intersection of the closure of S with the closure of its complement.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="frontier_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="setdiff"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Rewrite the complement of the interior as the closure of the complement.
sketch_steps: translate: The boundary is cl(S) minus int(S).
derive: The complement of int(S) equals cl(S^c).
conclude: Substituting gives cl(S) ∩ cl(S^c).

drafts.canonical_statement: A map f from X to Y is continuous if and only if the preimage of every closed subset of Y is closed in X.

drafts.proof_strategy: Translate between open and closed sets through complements of preimages.
sketch_steps: translate: Continuity means preimages of open sets are open.
derive: Preimages commute with complements.
conclude: The open-set and closed-set conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: A map f is continuous if and only if f(cl S) is contained in cl(f(S)) for every subset S.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the closed preimage of cl(f(S)) forward, and test on S = f^{-1}(C) backward.
sketch_steps: case_split: Prove the two implications separately.
derive: If f is continuous, the preimage of cl(f(S)) is closed and contains S.
apply_theorem: Minimality of the closure gives f(cl S) ⊆ cl(f S).
construct: Conversely set S = f^{-1}(C) for a closed set C.
conclude: Then cl(S) ⊆ S, so preimages of closed sets are closed.

drafts.canonical_statement: A map between metric spaces is continuous if and only if it sends every sequence converging to a to a sequence converging to f(a).

drafts.proof_strategy: Forward by neighborhoods; backward by choosing a witness sequence from the failure of epsilon-delta.
sketch_steps: case_split: Prove the two implications separately.
derive: Continuity pulls a neighborhood of f(a) back to a neighborhood of a.
contradiction: Assume f is discontinuous at a with witness ε.
construct: Choose a_n within 1/(n+1) of a with d(f(a_n), f(a)) ≥ ε.
conclude: The sequence converges to a but its image does not converge to f(a).

drafts.proof_strategy: Translate preimages of balls into balls contained in preimages.
sketch_steps: derive: The preimage of an ε-ball at f(b) is open and contains a δ-ball at b.
setup: Conversely fix an open set V and a point b of its preimage.
derive: Choose ε with the ε-ball inside V and take the matching δ.
conclude: The δ-ball lies in the preimage, so the preimage is open.

drafts.proof_strategy: The agreement set is closed and contains a dense set.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The agreement set E of f and g is closed since Y is Hausdorff.
derive: E contains S, hence contains the closure of S.
conclude: The closure of S is X, so f = g.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a homeomorphism h, the image h(U) is open if and only if U is open.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="homeomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="open_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="image_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="open_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Express the image as a preimage under the inverse map.
sketch_steps: translate: The image h(U) is the preimage of U under the inverse of h.
derive: Continuity of the inverse gives one implication.
derive: U = h^{-1}(h(U)) and continuity of h give the other.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.

drafts.proof_strategy: Show f is a closed map via closed subset, continuous image and compact-in-Hausdorff.
sketch_steps: translate: It suffices that f sends closed sets to closed sets.
derive: A closed subset C of the compact space X is compact.
derive: f(C) is compact as a continuous image.
apply_theorem: A compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed.
conclude: f is a closed bijection, so its inverse is continuous.

drafts.canonical_statement: If B is a basis, a set S is open if and only if every point a of S lies in some member t of B with t contained in S.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the description of open sets as unions of basis members.
sketch_steps: derive: An open S is a union of basis members, which gives t for each point.
derive: Conversely S is the union of the members t chosen for its points.
conclude: Unions of open sets are open.

drafts.canonical_statement: A second countable space has a countable dense subset.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="second_countable_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="countable_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dense_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Choose one point from each nonempty member of a countable basis.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a countable basis of X.
construct: Pick one point from each nonempty basis member to form D.
derive: Each nonempty open set contains a nonempty basis member, hence a point of D.
conclude: D is countable and dense.

drafts.canonical_statement: A separable metric space is second countable.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="metric_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="separable_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="second_countable_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use rational balls centered on a countable dense subset.
sketch_steps: setup: Take a countable dense subset D of X.
construct: Let B be the balls with center in D and positive rational radius.
derive: B is countable.
derive: For x in open U choose rational r with B(x,2r) ⊆ U and c in D near x.
conclude: x ∈ B(c,r) ⊆ U, so B is a basis.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a second countable space, every family of open sets has a countable subfamily with the same union.

drafts.proof_strategy: Index the subfamily by the countable basis members lying inside some U_i.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a countable basis B.
construct: Let B' be the members of B contained in some U_i and pick one such i for each.
derive: The chosen index set T is countable.
derive: Each point of the union lies in a member of B' and so in some U_j with j in T.
conclude: The two unions agree.

drafts.canonical_statement: A subset V of a subspace A of X is open in A if and only if V is the trace on A of an open subset of X.

drafts.proof_strategy: Unfold the subspace topology as the topology induced by the inclusion.
sketch_steps: translate: The subspace topology is induced by the inclusion map.
derive: The preimage of U under the inclusion is U ∩ A.
conclude: Open sets of A are exactly the traces of open sets of X.

drafts.canonical_statement: A map into a product of two spaces is continuous if and only if both components are continuous.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="continuous_between"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="product_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="continuous_between"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="function_compose_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="projection_first"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="continuous_between"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="function_compose_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="projection_second"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Check continuity on the product basis.
sketch_steps: derive: Composing with continuous projections gives continuous components.
setup: Conversely consider a basic open set U × V.
derive: Its preimage is the intersection of the component preimages.
conclude: Preimages of basis members are open, so f is continuous.

drafts.canonical_statement: The closure of a product set equals the product of the closures.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="product_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="product_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="product_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closure_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Test membership in the closure on basic neighborhoods U × V.
sketch_steps: translate: Use the characterization of closure by basic neighborhoods U × V.
derive: (U × V) ∩ (S × T) equals (U ∩ S) × (V ∩ T).
derive: This set is nonempty exactly when both factors are nonempty.
conclude: Hence (x,y) ∈ cl(S × T) iff x ∈ cl(S) and y ∈ cl(T).

drafts.canonical_statement: If q from X to Y is a quotient map, then g from Y to Z is continuous if and only if g composed with q is continuous.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="topological_quotient_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="continuous_between"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="continuous_between"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="function_compose_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the defining property of quotient maps on preimages.
sketch_steps: derive: Composition with the continuous map q gives one direction.
setup: Conversely fix an open set V of Z.
derive: The preimage of g^{-1}(V) under q is the preimage of V under the composite.
conclude: By definition of the quotient topology g^{-1}(V) is open.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the definition of compactness to the given cover.
sketch_steps: setup: Regard the family as an open cover of K.
conclude: Compactness extracts a finite subfamily still covering K.

drafts.canonical_statement: A closed subset of a compact set is compact.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closed_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Add the complement of C to the cover and use compactness of K.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix an open cover of C.
construct: Add the open set C^c to get an open cover of K.
apply_theorem: Extract a finite subcover of K.
conclude: Removing C^c leaves a finite subcover of C.

drafts.canonical_statement: The image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="continuous_between"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="image_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Pull the cover back, extract a finite subcover and push it forward.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix an open cover of f(K).
derive: The preimages form an open cover of K.
apply_theorem: Compactness of K gives a finite subcover of preimages.
conclude: The corresponding open sets cover f(K).

drafts.canonical_statement: A compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed.

drafts.proof_strategy: Separate x from each point of K and use a finite subcover.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix x outside K.
apply_theorem: For each y in K choose disjoint open U_y ∋ x and V_y ∋ y.
derive: Finitely many V_y cover K by compactness.
derive: The finite intersection of the corresponding U_y is an open neighborhood of x missing K.
conclude: The complement of K is open.

drafts.proof_strategy: The image is compact in ℝ, so it contains its supremum and infimum.
sketch_steps: derive: f(K) is a nonempty compact subset of ℝ.
apply_theorem: Compact subsets of ℝ are closed and bounded.
derive: The supremum and infimum exist and lie in f(K).
conclude: Points of K attaining them give the maximum and minimum.

drafts.canonical_statement: The product of an arbitrary family of compact spaces is compact in the product topology.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use ultrafilters and componentwise convergence (outline).
sketch_steps: translate: Compactness is equivalent to convergence of every ultrafilter.
setup: Take an ultrafilter F on the product.
derive: Each projection of F is an ultrafilter on X_i and has a limit x_i.
construct: Choose the limits to form a point x of the product.
conclude: Componentwise convergence gives F converging to x.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take complements to obtain an open cover and argue by contradiction.
sketch_steps: contradiction: Assume the full intersection with K is empty.
translate: The complements of the C_i form an open cover of K.
apply_theorem: Extract a finite subcover.
conclude: A finite intersection with K is empty, contradicting the hypothesis.

drafts.canonical_statement: A compact subset of a metric space is closed and bounded.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="metric_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closed_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="bounded_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Hausdorffness gives closedness; a cover by balls gives boundedness.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Metric spaces are Hausdorff, so K is closed.
construct: Cover K by the balls B(a,n) centered at a point a.
derive: Finitely many balls suffice, so K lies in one ball.
conclude: K is bounded.

drafts.canonical_statement: A compact Hausdorff space is normal.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="hausdorff_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Closed subsets are compact, then separate disjoint compact sets.
sketch_steps: setup: Take disjoint closed sets A and B.
derive: They are compact as closed subsets of a compact space.
apply_theorem: Disjoint compact sets in a Hausdorff space are separated by open sets.
conclude: X is normal.

drafts.canonical_statement: A continuous map from a compact metric space to a metric space is uniformly continuous.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="metric_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="metric_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="continuous_between"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="uniformly_continuous_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use a finite subcover to take a uniform δ.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix ε > 0 and pick δ_x from continuity at each point x.
apply_theorem: Compactness gives a finite subcover by the balls B(x, δ_x).
construct: Let δ be the minimum of the finitely many δ_{x_i}.
derive: Points within δ both lie within 2δ_{x_i} of a common center x_i.
conclude: The triangle inequality gives d(f(y), f(z)) < ε.

drafts.proof_strategy: Minimize the continuous positive function x ↦ d(x,C) on K.
sketch_steps: setup: Dispose of the trivial cases where K or C is empty.
derive: x ↦ d(x,C) is continuous and positive on K since C is closed and disjoint from K.
apply_theorem: The extreme value theorem gives a positive minimum r on K.
conclude: Hence d(x,y) ≥ d(x,C) ≥ r for x in K and y in C.

drafts.canonical_statement: A subset K of a metric space is compact if and only if every sequence in K has a subsequence converging to a point of K.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="metric_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sequentially_compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compactness gives cluster points; conversely use total boundedness and a Lebesgue number (outline).
sketch_steps: contradiction: A sequence without convergent subsequence contradicts a finite cover by small balls.
derive: Sequential compactness implies total boundedness via ε-separated sequences.
derive: Sequential compactness gives a Lebesgue number for any open cover.
construct: Take a finite δ-net for the Lebesgue number δ.
conclude: Each ball of the net lies in a cover member, giving a finite subcover.

drafts.canonical_statement: A subset of Euclidean space ℝ^n is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.

drafts.proof_strategy: Enclose K in a cube, which is a finite product of compact intervals.
sketch_steps: derive: Compact implies closed and bounded in any metric space.
setup: Conversely enclose a closed bounded K in a cube [-R,R]^n.
apply_theorem: Closed intervals are compact and finite products of compact sets are compact.
conclude: K is a closed subset of a compact set, so it is compact.
